findings.problem: Greek has a lacuna marked *** : 'στρατηγεῖν μὲν γὰρ ... δυνατὸς ἦν, καὶ *** ἀνδρώδης ὑπῆρχε τῇ φύσει'. The English reads on as if the clause were whole; the gap is smoothed over.

units.note: Greek breaks off at 'προχειρότερος ἐγίνετο πρὸς τὰς' and the English completes it from the next chapter's opening (ξενικὰς καὶ στρατιωτικὰς χάριτας); acceptable seam, not flagged.

findings.quote: and increasingly contrasted him with Sosibius
findings.problem: Greek: 'τὸν δὲ Σωσίβιον ἐκ παραθέσεως ἐθαύμαζον' - they ADMIRED Sosibius by comparison. The English drops the admiration (ἐθαύμαζον) and invents 'increasingly'; the next sentence (ἐδόκει γὰρ οὗτος ...) gives the grounds for the admiration.

units.note: ἐξήλεγξαν τὰς ἐλπίδας is somewhat uncertain in sense; English 'proved stronger than every expectation' is not clearly wrong, so left alone.

findings.quote: the people of Mylae, Alabanda, and Magnesia
findings.problem: Greek 'Μυλασεῖς' = people of Mylasa in Caria (not Mylae, a Sicilian place).
findings.proposed_fix: the people of Mylasa, Alabanda, and Magnesia

findings.problem: Greek 'ἐπὶ τὴν Μυλασέων πόλιν' = the city of Mylasa.

findings.quote: For he was well aware of the embassies being sent to Rome against him, now that affairs in Libya had come to an end.
findings.problem: Greek has a lacuna (* and ** ) after 'πρεσβείας εἰς Ῥώμην,' before 'διόπερ πέρας ἔχει τὰ κατὰ τὴν Λιβύην' ('therefore the affairs in Libya come to an end'). The English joins them as a seamless sentence and turns 'διόπερ' into a causal 'now that', smoothing the gap.
findings.proposed_fix: For he was well aware of the embassies being sent to Rome against him, [text missing] ... hence the affairs in Libya were at an end.

units.note: The book number in the Polybius fragment is garbled in the Greek (ι#2#); English 'sixteenth' is a reasonable reading, not flagged. Fragment of Strabo/Athenaeus-type excerpting; the Greek is also textually uncertain around the lacuna.
